find_gem_names.description: Find gem names that match some text, from the same lookup that fills the search box on RubyGems.org. Names only, which is what 'is there a gem called something like this?' asks and what feeds a gem field in a later step. The answer says whether one of them matched exactly. No API key required.
find_gem_names.name: find_gem_names

parameters.description: The beginning of a gem name. Matching is on the name itself, not on descriptions, so a topic finds nothing here and belongs in 'Search gems'.
parameters.name: query

parameters.description: How many rows to return, from 1 to 500. The answer always says how many there were in total, so a limited list never reads as a complete one. Defaults to 25.
parameters.name: limit

get_gem.description: Look up a gem on RubyGems.org: what it does, who wrote it, what licence it carries, where its source, issues and changelog live, what it depends on, and how often it has been downloaded. Everything is at the gem's newest release; use 'Get a gem version' to read an older one. No API key required.

parameters.description: The gem to look up, spelled exactly as you would install it. Use 'Find gem names' first if you are not sure of the spelling.

get_gem_downloads.description: Get how often one release of a gem was downloaded, and how often the gem has been downloaded in total. Both numbers come back together with the release's share worked out, so a step can report adoption of a new version without a second call. No API key required.
get_gem_downloads.name: get_gem_downloads

parameters.description: The gem to look up, spelled exactly as you would install it. Use 'Find gem names' first if you are not sure of the spelling.
parameters.name: gem

parameters.description: Which release to read. Fill in the gem first and this list loads, newest first, with the date each went out. Yanked releases are not listed, because RubyGems no longer serves them.
parameters.name: version

parameters.description: Which build of this release to read. Leave blank for the default, which is the pure Ruby build for almost every gem. Fill in the gem and version first and this list loads.
parameters.name: platform

get_gem_version.description: Read one specific release of a gem in full: its summary and description, when it was built and published, the Ruby and RubyGems versions it needs, its dependencies and its checksums. Use it to read the release a project actually pins rather than whatever is newest today. No API key required.

Versions order by RubyGems' own rules rather than as text, so 1.10.0 sits above 1.9.0 and a release above its own release candidates. Only indexed releases are listed, so a yanked one is absent. No API key required.

description: Read anything on RubyGems.org. Look a gem up by name for its licence, authors, links and dependencies, walk its whole release history, open one release for its files, checksums and signed attestations, and see who can push to it. Search the registry, watch what has been published in the last week, find which gems depend on one you care about, and track download counts for a release, a gem or the whole site. No account or API key is required.
